title: Jacob’s words recorded
summary: Nephi says Jacob spoke many more things to his people, but Nephi wrote only these things.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob spoke many more things to Nephi’s people at that time.
Nephi says he caused only these things to be written.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Jacob may be shown among a people, though the verse does not specify where or whether they are together at the moment of writing.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, appearance of the people, and the writing medium are not stated.

narration.text: Jacob spake many more things to my people at that time
only these things have I caused to be written

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict additional words spoken by Jacob; their content is not supplied.

title: Nephi writes of Isaiah
summary: Nephi says he writes more of Isaiah’s words, delights in them, and will send Isaiah’s and Jacob’s words to his children as witnesses.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi writes more of Isaiah’s words and delights in them.
Nephi says Isaiah saw his Redeemer, as Nephi has seen him.
Nephi says Jacob has also seen him, and that he will send their words to his children as proof.
Nephi says God establishes his word by the words of three, sends more witnesses, and proves all his words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi can be shown writing; the verse does not describe the setting or writing materials.
unspecified_visual_details: Isaiah and Jacob are mentioned as witnesses but are not described as present.

narration.text: I, Nephi, write more of the words of Isaiah
he verily saw my Redeemer, even as I have seen him
my brother, Jacob, also has seen him as I have seen him
by the words of three, God hath said, I will establish my word

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Redeemer’s appearance is not described in these verses; do not depict him.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Isaiah or Jacob as physically present in Nephi’s writing scene.

title: Nephi’s testimony of Christ
summary: Nephi expresses delight in proving Christ’s coming, in the Lord’s covenants and attributes, and in the need for Christ; he affirms that God is Christ and that Christ will come in his own time.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi delights in proving the truth of Christ’s coming and says the law of Moses and all things given by God from the beginning typify him.
Nephi delights in the Lord’s covenants, grace, justice, power, mercy, and plan of deliverance from death.
Nephi says that without Christ all men must perish.
Nephi says that without Christ there is no God or creation; he affirms that there is a God, that he is Christ, and that Christ comes in the fulness of his own time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown writing or reflecting on these teachings; no specific action is described.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible depiction of Christ, the law of Moses, creation, death, or deliverance is described.

narration.text: my soul delighteth in proving unto my people the truth of the coming of Christ
my soul delighteth in his grace, and in his justice, and power, and mercy
save Christ should come all men must perish
there is a God, and he is Christ
he cometh in the fulness of his own time

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements about Christ, death, creation, and deliverance are teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict symbolic events or visions as literal scenes.

title: Nephi introduces Isaiah’s words
summary: Nephi says he writes some of Isaiah’s words so that those who see them may lift their hearts and rejoice.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi writes some of Isaiah’s words, intending that those who see them may lift their hearts and rejoice for all men.
Nephi says the words may be likened to the readers and to all men.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, writing medium, and readers are not described.

narration.text: I write some of the words of Isaiah
may lift up their hearts and rejoice for all men
ye may liken them unto you and unto all men

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a gathering of readers or depict Isaiah as present.
